messages:
maria: FYI CI just failed on publishflow for the samplekit package. Looks like a regen diff but the diff is only a one-line timestamp in CHANGELOG.md header :/
kevin: ugh that again. which pipeline? openapi -> typegen -> publish?
maria: openapi -> codegen -> typegen -> publish. The failing job is `npm:publish` after typegen artifacts uploaded. ci-bot posted the npm error.
ci-bot: :x: publish failed for @redwood/samplekit@1.4.2 - 409 version already exists (registry reject)
jenna: 409 usually means semver/version bump mismatch. but you said regen diff is just a timestamp?
maria: exactly. typegen output contains a generated changelog entry with an RFC3339-ish timestamp. Our release stamp uses `now` during regen, so every run can change the timestamp even if nothing else changed. CI treats that as a gen diff and blocks publishing because we require zero-diff for release branches.
sam: ah the infamous "timestamp ghost". We had a quick fix in a hack branch before: normalize times to commit date. But that broke local dev flows.
kevin: Where's the offending file? path?
maria: packages/samplekit/CHANGELOG.md entry header: `## 1.4.2 - 2026-10-12T14:05:23Z` changed to `2026-10-12T14:07:45Z` between runs.
jenna: Could we have the CI regen step use `GIT_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP` from the CI env instead of wallclock? That keeps builds reproducible.
sam: +1. Another option: add a `--stable-timestamps` flag to the generator that reads `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` if present (like other reproducible tools).
kevin: We're also seeing flaky auth/retry test failures in the sample app tests tied to publish step timing out when the publish-bot retries auth. Not sure if related but seen in same run.
maria: I think they're related only by timing — publish blocked because 409, then publish-bot retried, then some test harness that expected a new package id timed out. Separate but cascading.
jenna: Proposed action: 1) short-term patch: make regen use SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (CI sets it from commit timestamp) 2) add guard to publish job: if regen-only diff is timestamp-only, treat as no-op for release branch 3) long-term: switch changelog generator to use semantic entries (no fresh timestamp unless content changed). Thoughts?
sam: I can do (1) today. Small env var change in the Dockerfile and a tiny generator flag.
kevin: I'll prototype detection for (2) — a script that `git diff --unified=0` and checks for regex that matches only timestamp lines in changelog. If found, exit 0 and log a note.
maria: sounds good. For (3) maybe product/pm alignment needed; but agree it's cleaner.
jenna: Can we also add an integration test that runs regen twice and asserts no diffs if no code changes? That would catch regressions.
sam: adding test now. Will open a PR with `ci: regen use SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and a link when ready.
kevin: I'll open a follow-up PR for the diff-detect guard and the flaky auth retry backoff tweak for publish-bot (increase backoff and add a deterministic jitter).
maria: thanks all. tagging @devex for visibility. :raised_hands:
ci-bot: Attached logs: https://ci.example.com/build/2775839123/logs (artifact: packages/samplekit/CHANGELOG.diff)
